title: DoMe relay WebSocket frames
description: All frames are JSON objects with a `type`. Frames are limited to 65536 bytes. Unknown `type` or unknown fields are rejected with MALFORMED_MESSAGE and the socket may be closed. The relay never alters a signed envelope or a challenge_text; it adds routing metadata in sibling fields which receivers treat as informational only. Terminal-result rule: every command_id a controller sends ends with exactly one `result` frame (see version.json rules.terminal_result); `error` frames are for situations with no command_id. Close codes: 1009 frame too large; 4000 protocol error; 4001 superseded by another connection of the same PC (the agent must NOT auto-reconnect; it shows a tray warning with a manual Reconnect); 4003 revoked/unauthorised; 4008 authentication required.

kid.description: REQUIRED when component is 'controller': the installation's controller key id. The relay binds the socket to the controller row (session account, kid); every envelope on this socket must carry the same kid.

proof.description: Controller sockets only. An ES256 envelope signed by the key named by `kid` whose payload is a `hello_proof` (#/$defs/hello_proof). The relay binds the socket to the controller row only after verifying it; a hello without a valid proof stays unbound (hello_ack without controller_id). Agents never send it (they authenticate with the PC access token).

hello.description: First frame on every socket. Controller sockets MUST include kid (bound to the session's account); agent sockets are identified by their bearer token.

hello_ack.description: controller_id is present on controller sockets whose kid matched a non-revoked controller of the account; a socket without controller_id may only be used to poll pairing status via REST, never for subscribe/command/confirmation/cancel (those answer error GRANT_MISSING). pc_id is present on agent sockets and must equal the agent's stored identity.

ref_pc_id.description: Required for subscription errors so the controller knows which PC was refused

ref_input_session_id.description: Manual-input rejections (INPUT_*, and since 1.4 the Screen view rejections of input batches SCREEN_SESSION_REQUIRED / SCREEN_GEOMETRY_CHANGED): the input session the refused batch named. The phone ignores errors for a session it no longer runs.

ref_controller_id.description: Agent → relay only, on INPUT_* and SCREEN_* rejections: the controller whose batch was refused. The relay routes the frame to that controller's sockets of a compatible version (1.1 for INPUT_*, 1.4 for SCREEN_*; after checking the controller belongs to the PC's account) and strips this field.

error_frame.description: Relay or agent → peer. Used only when no command_id can be associated (malformed frame, protocol incompatibility, subscription errors, manual-input batch rejections). Command-scoped failures are always `result` frames.

controller_subscribe.description: Controller → relay. Idempotent; REPLACES the socket's subscription set (subscriptions never survive a socket). Each pc_id must be a PC of the session's account on which THIS controller (bound at hello) holds a live grant; otherwise error{GRANT_MISSING, ref_pc_id} for that id and no subscription. For each accepted id the relay sends pc_status and then the cached last `state` frame of that PC (unchanged, with its original `at`) when one exists.

controller_command.description: Controller → relay. The relay verifies the envelope signature against the controller's registered key, checks the payload's account/controller/target ownership and grant, enforces rate limits and queue depth, then forwards to the PC. It never executes anything itself.

controller_cancel.description: Controller → relay → PC. Best-effort cancel of a queued or countdown command. Not signed in v1.0 because the worst case is a cancelled action; the relay checks the controller owns the command.

granted_until.description: End of the first allowance ticket; null only when unlimited is true.

stun_urls.description: STUN only: the PC never holds a TURN credential (rules.screen_signaling).

relayed_max_kbps.description: Present when the relay asks for Data saver on relayed paths (the monthly TURN guard, rules.screen_metering).

screen.description: Since 1.4, present only on a forwarded screen.session_start: the first allowance ticket and the PC's STUN servers (rules.screen_sessions / screen_signaling). Absent on every other command.

grants_snapshot.description: Relay → agent, sent immediately after hello_ack and whenever grants change. The agent applies it BEFORE accepting commands after (re)connect. It is a revocation/intersection list over the PC's LOCALLY approved controllers: a controller is usable only if locally approved AND listed here; effective capabilities = local ∩ snapshot. It carries no public keys and can never add a controller or widen a grant. A listed controller_id/kid the PC does not know locally is ignored and reported as a security event. pc_enabled=false or status=plan_disabled are plan/account states, not revocations: local grants stay, commands are refused with PC_PLAN_DISABLED / CONTROLLER_PLAN_DISABLED.

pc_enabled.description: False when the PC is disabled by the account or by the plan after a downgrade; the agent then refuses every command with PC_PLAN_DISABLED (local emergency controls still work)

status.description: plan_disabled keeps the LOCAL grant intact (revocation/emergency stop keep working) but the PC refuses commands with CONTROLLER_PLAN_DISABLED

entitlement_assertion.description: Compact JWS (EdDSA) or absent on Free

pairing_request.description: Relay → agent. A signed-in controller claimed this PC's pairing code (by hash). Delivered immediately when the agent is online and re-delivered, for every unexpired claimed pairing session of this PC, right after grants_snapshot on each (re)connect. The agent MUST recompute kid_from_jwk(public_jwk) and refuse on mismatch, then compute the verification code HMAC(code, pairing_id|pc_id|kid) locally and show it with controller_display_name (untrusted text) for the user to approve or decline.

code_hash.description: SHA-256 handle of the pairing code the PC is displaying; the agent ignores requests whose code_hash does not match its current pairing session

pairing_decision.description: Agent → relay after the local approve/decline. On approve, `kid` must equal the kid the agent computed from the JWK it stored; the relay only then creates the controller/grant rows. Since 1.4 an approve carries pc_key_mac (rules.pc_key_pinning); the relay stores it and returns it with the PC's public key in pairing_status_response.pc_key once approved. Agents older than 1.4 send none, and such a pairing cannot use Screen view until the phone pairs again.

pc_key_mac.description: base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key = normalised pairing code, msg = 'dome-pair-pc-key-v1|' + pairing_id + '|' + pc_id + '|' + controller_kid + '|' + pc_kid)), 32 bytes untruncated. Only on approve.

agent_ack.description: Agent → relay → controller. Delivery/authorization acknowledgement only; NOT an execution result. Never carries a terminal state.

agent_confirmation_required.description: Agent → relay → controller. `challenge_text` is the PC's compact JSON serialisation of a `challenge` object, carried as an opaque string. The relay strict-parses a copy to validate it against #/$defs/challenge and forwards the ORIGINAL string verbatim; the controller strict-parses it once for display and hashes the string verbatim for confirmation.challenge_digest.

challenge.description: Issued by the PC and serialised ONCE into confirmation_required.challenge_text. `display.detail` and anything derived from window/tab titles is UNTRUSTED text: the controller renders the primary line from `action`/`params`/`target` using its own registry labels, shows the PC name from its own device inventory matched by `pc_id`, and renders `display.detail` as plain text in a secondary style. `action_label` is a hint only. The confirmation envelope must be signed by the same kid as the original command; the PC records that kid on the challenge.

target_state_digest.description: base64url SHA-256 of the relevant target state (e.g., window title + handle) at challenge time; the PC re-checks before executing

agent_result.description: Terminal execution result. origin `agent` when produced by the PC, `relay` when the relay had to terminate the command itself (pre-forward rejection, PC offline, connection lost after forwarding → outcome_unknown).

result.description: Action-specific resulting state (e.g. new video id, volume)

warning.description: e.g. 'A previous Next may have executed before the connection dropped'

agent_state.description: Agent → relay → subscribed controllers. Periodic and on-change PC state. Media titles are untrusted display data.

input_session.description: The live manual-input session on this PC, if any.

input_restricted.description: True while the agent knows injection would be refused (locked session, secure desktop, elevated foreground).

tab_token.description: Present when script_attached; changes on every content-script attach

script_attached.description: False means the tab exists but DoMe's content script is not running in it (reload needed); such a tab cannot be a target

context.description: Page kind. Orthogonal flags below refine it.

pc_status_event.description: Relay → controller. Connection-level status the relay knows (not execution state). `last_seen` is the last frame received from the PC.

revoked.description: Relay → controller when this controller's grant or session was revoked; the socket closes afterwards.

agent_revoke_controller.description: Agent → relay. The PC owner revoked a controller locally (tray). The relay revokes the grant, sends `revoked` to that controller's sockets and a fresh grants_snapshot back.

agent_revoked.description: Relay → agent. This PC's cloud access is gone. The agent must stop reconnecting, discard the PC credential, keep local grants for the user to inspect, and show a local re-link prompt.

hello_proof.description: Payload of hello.proof. Proves to the relay that the socket's owner holds the controller key before the socket is bound to the paired controller (a bare kid is public to the whole account). Verifier checks: signature with the JWK the relay stored at pairing for (session account, kid); envelope.kid == kid == hello.kid; account_id == the session's account; issued_at/expires_at within the normal window with lifetime <= confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds; nonce not seen before on this relay (single use).

elevated.description: True when the agent could determine the foreground window belongs to a higher-integrity process (input will be refused by Windows).

foreground_app.description: What the PC has in front, as far as the agent can observe. Field-level focus inside the window is not observable and is never claimed.

oneOf.description: Relative cursor motion in desktop pixels; adjacent moves may be summed by the agent.
Wheel motion in notches; positive dy scrolls content up (wheel away from the user), matching Windows WHEEL_DELTA sign.
Literal committed text, inserted as Unicode; never parsed.
One press-and-release of a named key. f11 (since 1.4) toggles full screen in apps that are not approved; approved apps have app.set_fullscreen.
Tested shortcut; the modifier is released after the key. ctrl_l is the browser address bar and is only offered in browser contexts.

Since 1.4 (Screen view). Absolute cursor position normalised to 0..65535 over the streamed surface at geometry generation `gen`, never PC pixels; the PC maps it to physical pixels of that monitor. Needs a live screen session owned by the batch's controller (SCREEN_SESSION_REQUIRED) and gen == current (SCREEN_GEOMETRY_CHANGED). Within a batch the last position wins; never summed.

Since 1.4 (Screen view). Wheel motion in Windows wheel units (120 = one notch, |dx|,|dy| <= input_wheel_max) for smooth two-finger scrolling; positive dy scrolls content up, like pointer_scroll. Raw delta to MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL / HWHEEL.

input_batch_payload.description: Signed payload of a controller_input_batch envelope (rules.input_sessions). An empty events array renews the lease.

controller_input_batch.description: Controller → relay. Manual-input events for the PC's live input session; the relay verifies and forwards, never executes, journals or logs the content.

agent_input_ack.description: Agent → relay → the owning controller. Windows accepted these events (not an observed application effect); at most 4 per second per session.

agent_input_session.description: Agent → relay → controllers (the owner always; subscribers see the owner via pc_state.input_session). Session lifecycle: started, suspended (fresh start required) or ended with the reason; holds_released counts the buttons/keys this session still held and the agent released.

agent_grant_update.description: Agent → relay. The PC owner changed a controller's capabilities locally (rules.grant_update). The relay replaces the grant's capabilities with this list and pushes a fresh grants_snapshot.

screen_allowance_state.description: The Free allowance as the relay knows it (rules.screen_metering): unlimited: true on plans with screen_view_seconds_per_window null (then both other fields are null). Display only on the phone; the ledger is authoritative.

screen_rect.description: A rectangle normalised to 0..65535 over the streamed surface (the same units as pointer_move_to).

screen_ice_server.description: One RTCIceServer for the phone. A TURN entry carries a credential minted for this controller only, revoked by the relay on every §13 path (rules.screen_signaling). Never logged; never sent to the PC.

controller_screen_ice_request.description: Controller → relay (bound socket announcing 1.4). Ask for ICE servers and the current allowance before building the offer; the relay mints the phone's TURN credential here (rules.screen_signaling).

relay_screen_ice_servers.description: Relay → controller, the answer to screen_ice_request. turn: available (a TURN credential is in ice_servers), unavailable (no TURN key configured: STUN only) or disabled (a per-account cap or the monthly guard refused TURN: STUN only, the phone says so). A refusal of the request itself is an error frame (SCREEN_VIEW_DISABLED, SCREEN_ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED, GRANT_MISSING, PC_OFFLINE, PC_RECONNECTING, RATE_LIMITED, PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE) with ref_pc_id.

expires_at.description: When the TURN credential expires (TTL = remaining allowance + 60 s on Free, the session maximum on unlimited plans); null when no credential was minted.

screen_answer_payload.description: The payload the PC signs with its identity key (envelope kid = pc_kid) to answer one screen.session_start (rules.screen_signaling). offer_digest is base64url SHA-256 of the exact offer_sdp bytes it answers; answer_sdp is the send-only answer with the per-session DTLS fingerprint. Lifetime at most screen_answer_lifetime_seconds. Never journaled, never in a result.

agent_screen_answer.description: Agent → relay. The PC-signed answer (envelope over screen_answer_payload) for the controller named by ref_controller_id. The relay checks that this controller belongs to the PC's account and holds a live screen grant, strips ref_controller_id and delivers relay_screen_answer only to that controller's 1.4 sockets, preferring the one that issued the command; never to subscribers, never logged, no commands row.

relay_screen_answer.description: Relay → the issuing controller. The PC-signed answer, verbatim. The phone accepts it only under the checks of rules.screen_signaling (6) against the PC key pinned at pairing.

agent_screen_session.description: Agent → relay → the owner and the PC's 1.4 subscribers. Screen view lifecycle (rules.screen_sessions): started (after DTLS connected and the first frame was sent; `path` says whether media is direct or relayed), paused / resumed (reason secure_desktop or indicator) and ended with the reason. live_seconds is informational: the ledger is settled on the relay's clock. No names, no SDP, no addresses.

reason.description: `started` on event started; secure_desktop or indicator on paused / resumed; an end reason on ended.

path.description: On started (and resumed): how the media flows.

agent_screen_usage.description: Agent → relay, about screen_allowance_renew_before_seconds before the current ticket's granted_until (and at most twice per minute per session): ask for the next allowance chunk. live_seconds, relayed and relayed_bytes are informational only; the relay never charges or discounts on them (rules.screen_metering).

relay_screen_allowance.description: Relay → agent: the next allowance ticket, in answer to screen_usage or sent at once when the owning controller went offline (reason controller_offline). final: true means no further ticket will come; granted_until null with final means stop now. When granted_until passes without a new ticket the agent ends the session (rules.screen_sessions (4)).

screen_dc_phone_to_pc.description: Data-channel messages the phone may send (dome-screen-v1, DTLS-authenticated): hb renews the viewer lease, keyframe asks for an IDR, bye ends the session (`stopped`), audio{on} mutes or unmutes PC sound (Phase 2). Nothing here can inject input or run anything.

screen_dc_pc_to_phone.description: Data-channel messages the PC may send: geometry (a new generation: the streamed surface, its size and rotation, and DoMe's own reserved rectangles that taps must avoid), state (sending, or paused with the cause; encoder and data_saver as hints for the Health note and the badge), allowance (the ticket the PC last received, for the countdown) and restricted (input is currently refused on the PC and why). Phase 2/3 add cursor_shape, cursor_pos and roi.

screen_dc_message.description: Every message on the dome-screen-v1 data channel, in either direction (rules.screen_content): a JSON object of at most screen_dc_message_max_bytes with a closed vocabulary; each side validates against its own inbound direction (screen_dc_phone_to_pc on the PC, screen_dc_pc_to_phone on the phone) and drops anything else.
